title: Covenant
lead: A covenant (berit) is a binding agreement sealed by oath, between people or between God and people. The Bible's story is told through God's covenants with Noah, Abraham, Israel at Sinai and David, and the new covenant promised by Jeremiah and announced by Jesus (Jeremiah 31:31–34; Luke 22:20).

sections.b: God covenants with Noah and every living thing (Genesis 9:8–17), with Abraham to give him offspring and land (15:18; 17:1–14), with Israel at Sinai (Exodus 19–24), with Phinehas for priesthood (Numbers 25:12–13) and with David for a lasting dynasty (2 Samuel 7; Psalm 89:3–4). Human covenants and treaties appear too: Abraham and Abimelech (Genesis 21:27), Jacob and Laban (31:44), Jonathan and David (1 Samuel 18:3). Jeremiah promises a new covenant written on the heart (Jeremiah 31:31–34), which Jesus announces at the Last Supper (Luke 22:20; Hebrews 8:8–13).

sections.h: The new covenant in Jeremiah and Ezekiel
sections.b: Jeremiah 31:31–34 names the new covenant. Ezekiel holds its parts without the word: a covenant of peace (34:25; 37:26), a new heart and the LORD's own Spirit (36:24–28), and the command to get a new heart and a new spirit (18:31) beside the promise of a new heart (36:26). The command and the gift belong together.
